description:
🚀 Join Zero-G Cadets!
We're building the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer—a game where players survive on the Moon/Mars by managing life support, power, and food.

As an Environmental Engineer, I'm the "Chief Scientist" making the survival rules scientifically real.

We need:
• Game Devs (Unity/WebGL/Python)
• UI/UX Designers

You bring the code/art, I bring the science! Let's build!
summary:
"Beyond Earth" is a 3D browser-based survival game designed for kids aged 7–12. Players step into the boots of a Junior Astronaut managing an Artemis lunar outpost. The challenge is to balance three competing life-support resources—Power, Oxygen, and Crew Health—while surviving real-world space weather hazards.

What makes our game unique is its use of live NASA data. We integrated the NASA DONKI API to pull real solar flare data from the last 30 days. The in-game solar storm intensity (Class C, M, or X) directly scales the radiation damage, meteor showers, and power drain the player experiences. For the health mechanics, we modeled crew radiation exposure using biological constraints from the NASA OSDR (Open Science Data Repository).

Every decision in the game mirrors real mission planning: turning on the O2 recycler drains power, using the jetpack burns oxygen, and activating radiation shields drains the battery. Players must constantly make difficult trade-offs. With three difficulty modes (Cadet, Commander, Veteran), procedural Web Audio sound effects, and a fully playable 3D environment, Beyond Earth teaches the next generation of explorers that in space, no choice is free.
details:
Project Overview:
"Beyond Earth" is a 3D browser-based survival game for kids aged 7-12. Players manage an Artemis lunar outpost, balancing three critical resources: Power, Oxygen, and Crew Health. Every decision involves a real engineering trade-off—turning on the O2 recycler drains power, and activating radiation shields drains the battery even faster.

NASA Data Integration:
The game is powered by live NASA data. We integrated the NASA DONKI API to fetch real solar flare data from the last 30 days. The in-game solar storm intensity (Class C, M, or X) dynamically scales the radiation damage, meteor showers, and power drain. For crew health, we modeled radiation exposure using biological constraints from the NASA OSDR (Open Science Data Repository).

Technical Stack & Features:

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6).
  • 3D Engine: Three.js (WebGL) for lunar terrain, lighting, and particle effects.
  • Audio: Procedural Web Audio API (zero external audio assets, synthesized in real-time).
  • Gameplay: Includes a jetpack boost (consumes extra oxygen), meteor ground target rings, shield deflection mechanics, and three difficulty modes (Cadet, Commander, Veteran).

Source Code & Repository:
The complete source code, documentation, and project structure are publicly available on GitHub: https://github.com/engr-aimanafzal/Zero-G-Cadets

Creativity & Impact:
We designed the game to be accessible to young learners (plays instantly in any browser, no downloads) while teaching real space survival constraints. With live API data and dynamic difficulty, "Beyond Earth" ensures that in space, no choice is free.
